steps.message: Look at row 2, column 1. It has only one candidate: 8.
Because no other digit can go in row 2, column 1, place 8 there. This is called a Naked Single.

steps.message: In row 4, consider where 9 can appear.
Every other empty cell in row 4 cannot contain 9, leaving only row 4, column 4.
Because row 4 still needs 9 and row 4, column 4 is the only possible cell, place 9 there. This is called a Hidden Single.

steps.message: In column 2, the cells at row 4, column 2 and row 7, column 2 each have exactly the same two candidates: 1 and 3.
Those two cells must contain 1 and 3 in some order, so no other cell in column 2 can contain either digit.
Because those two cells reserve 1 and 3, remove candidate 1 from row 3, column 2; this deduction does not place a value. This pattern is called a Naked Pair.
